key_insight: The paper shows that topological crossover signatures in the Wen–plaquette model can still be resolved on noisy NISQ hardware by combining small-system characterization with a scalable hardware mapping.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route for testing and preparing robust topological states on near-term quantum processors despite disorder, circuit noise, and hardware imperfections.
method: Variationally compile equilibrium and quench-generated states on IBM Quantum hardware.
Measure local plaquette stabilizers and a Wilson loop to identify stabilizer-dominated versus trivial/disorder-dominated crossovers.
Scale from a small tractable system to a 2D IBM processor using a layered representative-qubit construction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resolved crossovers and robustness checks against static disorder, amplified circuit noise, and effective non-Hermitian fields, with the 2D hardware implementation showing only weak degradation under intentionally amplified local coherent perturbations.
watch_item: Results are still constrained by finite-size effects and the representativeness of the layered-qubit mapping, so scalability to larger fully connected topological systems remains to be validated.
paper_title: Resolving topological order crossovers on NISQ hardware
